```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lombard_2020_tumorsize_nsclc_local"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-020-04049-5> (open access, PMC7125250)
* Supplement (Online Resource: individual profiles, goodness-of-fit plots and
  prediction-corrected VPCs): available from the article page.

Lombard et al. studied how much the reader of a CT scan changes a tumour growth
inhibition (TGI) model. In a phase III trial of cisplatin alone versus
gemcitabine plus cisplatin in non-small cell lung cancer (Sandler 2000), the
same CT scans were measured twice: once by the radiologists of the treating
hospital ("local") and once at a centralised review centre ("central"). The
authors fitted the same Stein bi-exponential model (their Eq. 1) to each set of
readings separately, so the paper reports two parameter sets (Table 1). Both
are packaged:

* `Lombard_2020_tumorsize_nsclc_local` -- fitted to the hospital readings.
* `Lombard_2020_tumorsize_nsclc_central` -- fitted to the central readings.

```{r models}
mod_local <- readModelDb("Lombard_2020_tumorsize_nsclc_local")
mod_central <- readModelDb("Lombard_2020_tumorsize_nsclc_central")
rxode2::rxode(mod_local)$description
```

The model has no dose input. Both treatment arms were pooled without an arm
effect, so the decay rate `kse` (the paper's `Kd`, "drug effect") is the pooled
empirical shrinkage rate under platinum-based chemotherapy, and the growth
rate `kge` (`Kg`) is the rate of the treatment-resistant fraction.

# Population

The analysis used a subset of the trial: 120 lesions in 62 of the 522 patients,
selected because the same CT scan had been measured at both sites. This gives
714 observations (357 paired measurements), on average 3 (1-5) time points per
lesion with a median of 59 (19-116) days between measurements. Patients had
stage IIIA, IIIB or IV NSCLC and received cisplatin alone or gemcitabine plus
cisplatin for up to six cycles (August 1995 to February 1997, 28 sites).
Baseline longest diameters had a median of 3.0 cm (0.25-13.0) for the local and
2.8 cm (0.6-13.6) for the central readings, with a median of 2 (1-6) lesions per
patient. The unit of analysis is the individual lesion (individual longest
diameter, not the RECIST sum), so the random effects describe variability
between lesions. Age, sex and other demographics of the subset are not reported.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(mod_local)$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Local | Central | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TS = TS(0) * (exp(kge t) + exp(-kse t) - 1)` | -- | -- | Eq. 1 |
| `P_i = theta_P * exp(eta_i)` | -- | -- | Eq. 2 |
| `lrbase` (TS(0), cm) | log(3.1) | log(2.9) | Table 1 |
| `lkge` (Kg, 1/day) | log(0.0012) | log(0.00091) | Table 1 |
| `lkse` (Kd, 1/day) | log(0.0077) | log(0.0070) | Table 1 |
| `etalrbase` (variance) | 0.31 | 0.33 | Table 1, IIV-TS(0) |
| `etalkge` (variance) | 0.20 | 0.43 | Table 1, IIV-Kg |
| `etalkse` (variance) | 0.44 | 0.59 | Table 1, IIV-Kd |
| `addSd` (cm) | 0.43 | 0.40 | Table 1, additive residual error |

# Structural check: ODE solution against Eq. 1

The packaged model writes Eq. 1 as two exponential sub-states (`growth`,
`shrink`) that share the initial value TS(0). The solved typical-value
trajectory must reproduce the closed form to numerical precision.

```{r closed-form}
times <- seq(0, 730, by = 5)
typ <- function(mod, set) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = rxode2::et(times)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(set = set)
}
sim_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(typ(mod_local, "Local"), typ(mod_central, "Central"))

closed <- function(t, ts0, kg, kd) ts0 * (exp(kg * t) + exp(-kd * t) - 1)
chk <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    eq1 = ifelse(
      set == "Local",
      closed(time, 3.1, 0.0012, 0.0077),
      closed(time, 2.9, 0.00091, 0.0070)
    )
  )
max(abs(chk$TS - chk$eq1))
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is solver error only.
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$TS - chk$eq1)) < 1e-4)
```

# Typical lesion trajectories

```{r typical-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, TS, colour = set)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Longest diameter (cm)", colour = "Reader",
    title = "Typical-lesion longest diameter, local vs central fit",
    caption = "Typical values of Lombard 2020 Table 1 through Eq. 1."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Checks against values quoted in the paper

The Discussion converts the population rate constants into a halving time for
the decay (3.0 months local, 3.3 months central) and a doubling time for the
growth (19 months local, 25 months central), and Table 1 gives the relative
error ratio (RER, Eq. 3: difference over mean, in %) between the local and
central population estimates. Both follow directly from the packaged values.

```{r quoted-values}
pars <- function(mod) {
  ini <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
  th <- setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
  c(
    ts0 = exp(th[["lrbase"]]), kg = exp(th[["lkge"]]),
    kd = exp(th[["lkse"]]), sd = th[["addSd"]]
  )
}
p_loc <- pars(mod_local)
p_cen <- pars(mod_central)
days_per_month <- 365.25 / 12

halving <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Kd halving time (months)", "Kg doubling time (months)"),
  `Local (packaged)` = c(log(2) / p_loc[["kd"]], log(2) / p_loc[["kg"]]) / days_per_month,
  `Local (paper)` = c(3.0, 19),
  `Central (packaged)` = c(log(2) / p_cen[["kd"]], log(2) / p_cen[["kg"]]) / days_per_month,
  `Central (paper)` = c(3.3, 25)
)
knitr::kable(halving, digits = 2, caption = "Halving and doubling times (Lombard 2020 Discussion).")
stopifnot(
  abs(halving$`Local (packaged)` - halving$`Local (paper)`) < 0.1 * halving$`Local (paper)`,
  abs(halving$`Central (packaged)` - halving$`Central (paper)`) < 0.1 * halving$`Central (paper)`
)

rer <- tibble::tibble(
  Parameter = c("TS(0)", "Kg", "Kd", "Additive residual error"),
  Local = p_loc[c("ts0", "kg", "kd", "sd")],
  Central = p_cen[c("ts0", "kg", "kd", "sd")]
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `RER (packaged, %)` = (Local - Central) / ((Local + Central) / 2) * 100,
    `RER (Table 1, %)` = c(6, 28, 9, 7)
  )
knitr::kable(rer, digits = 4, caption = "Local-central relative error ratios (Lombard 2020 Table 1).")
# The paper's RERs come from unrounded estimates; recomputing them from the
# printed two-significant-figure values agrees to within about one point.
stopifnot(abs(rer$`RER (packaged, %)` - rer$`RER (Table 1, %)`) < 1.5)
```

The time of the typical nadir of a Stein trajectory is
`log(kse / kge) / (kge + kse)`; it is later for the central fit because its
growth rate is lower.

```{r nadir}
nadir <- function(p) log(p[["kd"]] / p[["kg"]]) / (p[["kg"]] + p[["kd"]])
tibble::tibble(
  Reader = c("Local", "Central"),
  `Typical nadir time (days)` = c(nadir(p_loc), nadir(p_cen)),
  `Typical nadir size (cm)` = c(
    closed(nadir(p_loc), p_loc[["ts0"]], p_loc[["kg"]], p_loc[["kd"]]),
    closed(nadir(p_cen), p_cen[["ts0"]], p_cen[["kg"]], p_cen[["kd"]])
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Virtual cohort and VPC

The supplement's prediction-corrected VPCs (Online Resource, panels A and B)
show observations up to about 220 days, binned at 0, 11-110 and 110-222 days.
A virtual set of 200 lesions per reader is simulated with an observation at
baseline and then roughly every 59 days (the median spacing in the data), with
log-normal inter-lesion variability and the additive residual error.

```{r vpc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200413)
n_lesion <- 200L
obs_times <- c(0, 59, 118, 177, 222)
ev <- rxode2::et(obs_times) |> rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_lesion))

sim_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_local, events = ev) |> as.data.frame() |> dplyr::mutate(set = "Local"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_central, events = ev) |> as.data.frame() |> dplyr::mutate(set = "Central")
)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(set, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = median(sim), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~set) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Longest diameter (cm)",
    title = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles",
    caption = "Compare with the prediction-corrected VPCs of the Lombard 2020 Online Resource."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The maintainers read the shaded 95% confidence intervals of the predicted
median and 95th percentile off the supplement VPCs (approximate, to about
0.2 cm). The typical-value trajectory is shown alongside the simulated median:
with log-normal variability on both rate constants the population median of a
Stein curve sits above the typical curve once growth starts to dominate, so it
is the simulated median, not the typical value, that is compared with the band.
Late bins in the data also hold only the lesions still being imaged, which the
simulation does not mimic.

```{r vpc-compare}
bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~set,      ~bin,      ~mid, ~med_lo, ~med_hi, ~p95_lo, ~p95_hi,
  "Local",   "0",          0,     2.6,     3.6,     7.1,    11.7,
  "Local",   "11-110",    59,     1.8,     2.5,     4.9,     9.2,
  "Local",   "110-222",  165,     1.6,     2.2,     4.2,     9.5,
  "Central", "0",          0,     2.4,     3.4,     6.7,    11.3,
  "Central", "11-110",    59,     1.7,     2.4,     4.8,     9.0,
  "Central", "110-222",  165,     1.5,     2.1,     4.1,     9.6
)
pv <- c(Local = list(p_loc), Central = list(p_cen))
bands$typical <- mapply(
  function(s, t) closed(t, pv[[s]][["ts0"]], pv[[s]][["kg"]], pv[[s]][["kd"]]),
  bands$set, bands$mid
)
sim_bins <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(time, c(-Inf, 11, 110, Inf), labels = c("0", "11-110", "110-222"))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(set, bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_median = median(sim), sim_p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
cmp <- bands |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_bins, by = c("set", "bin"))
cmp |>
  dplyr::select(
    Reader = set, `Bin (days)` = bin, `Typical value` = typical,
    `Median band lo` = med_lo, `Median band hi` = med_hi, `Simulated median` = sim_median,
    `95th band lo` = p95_lo, `95th band hi` = p95_hi, `Simulated 95th` = sim_p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated percentiles against the supplement VPC bands (maintainers' reading).")
# Centre-of-distribution check: the simulated median per bin lies within the
# band of the predicted median, widened by 0.3 cm for the reading precision and
# the Monte-Carlo error of a 200-lesion median.
stopifnot(all(cmp$sim_median >= cmp$med_lo - 0.3 & cmp$sim_median <= cmp$med_hi + 0.3))
```

The 95th-percentile band at baseline is what fixes the scale of the
inter-lesion variability: reading Table 1's IIV of TS(0) as a variance (0.31)
puts the typical 95th percentile at
`r round(3.1 * exp(qnorm(0.95) * sqrt(0.31)), 1)` cm, inside the 7.1-11.7 cm
band, while reading it as a standard deviation would put it at
`r round(3.1 * exp(qnorm(0.95) * 0.31), 1)` cm, well below the band.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 1 labels the variability rows only "IIV". They are read
  as NONMEM omega-squared variances. Two pieces of evidence support this: the
  baseline 95th-percentile band of the supplement VPCs (see above), and the
  spread of the individual TS(0), Kg and Kd estimates in Figure 3, which is
  wider than a standard deviation of 0.31 (TS(0)) would allow after shrinkage.
* **No drug input.** The paper pooled the cisplatin and gemcitabine plus
  cisplatin arms without an arm covariate and reports no exposure term, so the
  models carry no dose and `kse` is the pooled chemotherapy effect.
* **Values below the quantification limit.** About 10% of measurements were
  below 0.5 cm and were replaced by 0.25 cm before fitting. The packaged
  additive error model can simulate values below 0.5 cm or below zero; apply
  the same substitution to simulated data before comparing with observed data.
* **Lesion, not patient.** Each lesion was an individual in the fit (120 lesions
  in 62 patients); there is no patient-level random effect, so lesions of one
  patient are simulated as independent.
* **VPC bands.** The supplement VPC bands were read by eye; they are used only
  for a widened centre-of-distribution check and for display.
* **Reference.** The co-author surname is reproduced as printed in the article
  and its supplement ("Gueoguieva").
